title: Albert Cross Design Contest
High-Throughput Experimentation (HTE) Software for Drug Discovery
description: HTE is a field of chemistry that expanded exponentially in the past five years, and most pharmaceutical companies are currently using it in their workflows. This methodology allows multi-parameter optimisation of chemical reactions but also synthesis of multiple compounds (96 to 384) on a small-scale using plate chemistry. Combined with the implementation of Direct-to-Biology (D2B) approaches, which involves the direct testing of non-purified mixtures, biological data is obtained faster. The combination of these methods greatly improves the Design, Make, Test, and Analyse (DMTA) cycle.

buyer: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
title: Bulk Liquid Nitrogen (LN?) Delivery and Tank Rental Services
description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Clinical Center (CC), Department of Transfusion Medicine (DTM), Center for Cellular Engineering (CCE), intends to procure continued bulk liquid nitrogen (LN?) delivery and tank rental services from Roberts Oxygen Company, Inc. The requirement supports the existing bulk LN? system serving CCE's 3T cell-manufacturing facility in Building 10 at the NIH Clinical Center. The anticipated perio of performance is from 10/16/2026 to 09/30/2027. CCE manufactures human cell- and tissue-based products used in Phase I/II clinical protocols for transplantation, adoptive immunotherapy, and gene therapy and supports more than 30 patient-care clinical research protocols. The requirement includes bulk LN? deliveries to the existing tank located near the Building 10 Morgue and continued monthly rental of the installed tank. Basis for Intended Sole Source Roberts Oxygen Company, Inc. currently owns and provides the installed bulk LN? tank and supplies the liquid nitrogen used to support CCE's regulated cell-manufacturing and storage operations. The existing tank is installed on the NIH campus and connected to the CCE 3T cell-manufacturing facility. Changing suppliers would require removal of the existing tank and associated plumbing, installation of a new system, and requalification of the LN? source. Such a transition could result in additional costs and disruption to CCE's ability to manufacture and store cell therapy products. Additionally, Roberts Oxygen is currently the approved supplier for CCE manufacturing protocols. Use of an alternate supplier would require Quality Assurance review and requalification, potentially delaying patient treatment and ongoing clinical trials. Capability Statements This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, responsible sources that believe they can satisfy the Government's requirement may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required bulk LN? delivery and tank rental services. Capability statements should clearly demonstrate the vendor's ability to meet the requirement, including its ability to provide timely LN? deliveries, necessary supporting documentation for use in an FDA-regulated manufacturing environment, and any information demonstrating its ability to support the existing CCE operations. All capability statements must be received no later than October 16, 2026, at 8:00 AM Eastern Time (ET) and emailed to shasheshe.goolsby@nih.gov. The Government will consider all responses received by the stated deadline. A determination not to compete this proposed acquisition based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement.

title: Poskytování služeb agronomického poradenství v rámci vývoje analytiky chytrého zemědělství
description: Nalezení dodavatele služeb agronomického poradenství v rámci vývoje cenově dostupné analytiky chytrého zemědělství. Analytika vychází z atmosférických měření, půdních měření a dat dálkového průzkumu země. Účelem je, aby zadavatel získal odbornou agronomickou podporu při návrhu, volbě, ladění a validaci algoritmů a analytických modelů, poskytovanou formou konzultací, odborných stanovisek, doporučení a analýz. Podpora má povahu odborné duševní činnosti. Součástí není programování, implementace ani testování softwaru, provoz výpočetní techniky ani jiné poskytnutí strojového času, terénní měření, odběry vzorků, laboratorní nebo poloprovozní pokusy, pořízení hmotných věcí, licencí nebo dat od třetích osob ani jiné plnění, které nespočívá v odborné duševní činnosti osob dodavatele. Analytiku vyvíjí a algoritmy implementuje zadavatel vlastními silami. Zadavatel požaduje k výstupům služeb licenci v rozsahu, který umožní výstupy bez další součinnosti dodavatele užívat, upravovat, rozvíjet a komerčně využívat, a to bez územního, časového a množstevního omezení. Předmětem plnění jsou: 1) Pomoc s identifikací klíčových plodin a případů užití pro agroklimatické podmínky České republiky 2) Modelování závlahy a vodní bilance 3) Modelování výskytu chorob a škůdců 4) Modelování pro variabilně prováděné pěstební zásahy 5) Modelování fyziologie plodin 6) Modelování abiotických rizik

description: The purpose of Amendment 0001 is to provide answers to Offeror's J-5 Request for Clarifications Number 1-10. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 336611 (Ship Building and Repairing) and the Small Business Size Standard is 1,300 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) Code is J999 (Non-Nuclear Ship Repair (West)). The Government intends to award a firm fixed price (FFP) standalone contract that meets the specifications outlined below. The proposed contract action is for non-commercial supplies for which the Government intends to solicit as full and open competition. Interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement and submit proposals. Determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation without discussions to the responsible offeror whose proposal, conforming to the solicitation that represents the best value to the Government, price, delivery, technical acceptability, past performance, and other factors considered. Any questions received after this deadline may not be answered. Shipping terms shall be FOB Destination; therefore, proposal SHALL include ALL associated shipping costs, to include tariffs. Proposal must include price(s), FOB Destination, a point of contact, name and phone number, business size, and payment terms. An award will be made based on Best Value. Each proposal must clearly indicate the capability of the vendor to meet all specifications and/or requirements in the Statement of Work (SOW). Vendors shall provide a detailed (unpriced) capabilities statement for review and acceptance by the Technical POC. Responses to this solicitation are due by 0900 AM Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) on October 16, 2026. Please email proposals or requests for DoD SAFE submission links to: Bailey Butler: bailey.a.butler2.civ@us.navy.mil Shawn Comparto: shawn.k.comparto.civ@us.navy.mil Amber Hess: amber.e.hess3.civ@us.navy.mil Proposals shall be valid for one hundred eighty (180) days from the submission date (at minimum). See attached solicitation for a list of line item number(s) and items, quantities, and units of measure. The Point of Contact for this acquisition is Shawn Comparto, Contracting Officer. title: US Space Economy Study
description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION US SPACE ECONOMY STUDY This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with RFO Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and no other written solicitation will be issued. This solicitation is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ). Submit written quotes on RFQ Number 1305M427Q0003. This solicitation is being issued as a total small business set-aside. The associated NAICS code is 541720. The small business size standard is $28.0M. This combined solicitation/synopsis is for the following commercial services: Line Item 0001 � This study will identify and justify a set of defined metrics that can support recurring federal assessment and provide policymakers with sustained insight into the growth, health, competitiveness, resilience, and emerging challenges of the ecosystem, in accordance with the attached, incorporated Statement of Work. The period of performance for this contract shall not exceed 180 calendar days. Acquisition Framework: This commercial procurement is conducted under RFO Part 12, utilizing innovative techniques including an advisory down-select process and confidence ratings (see the Periodic Table of Acquisition Innovation for details). Two-Phase Strategy: To be considered for award, vendors must submit a Phase I quotation. Phase I Deadline: Phase I submissions must be uploaded via the designated Phase I Submission Form [https://forms.gle/rcKbAc4ZHDDn13YR9] no later than 9:00 AM ET October 16, 2026. Late submissions will not be evaluated. Phase II Timeline: The Government will establish the Phase II submission deadline within the advisory notifications issued after Phase I evaluations. Compliance: Quotations must be clear, concise, and fully compliant. Non-compliant submissions (e.g., missing documents, exceeding page limits, or violating formatting terms) may be excluded from evaluation. Solicitation Questions and Comments Questions and Comments regarding Phase I will not be accepted.

title: Professional Services Supply Chain
description: The CRA has issued this Request for Proposal (RFP) to solicit bids from qualified professional services suppliers for contracts under the Professional Services Supply Chain (PSSC). The PSSC is the CRA’s suite of contracts for the provision of IT and certain non-IT professional services. Bidders must be able to supply consultants for every category and level after award. All responsive bids will be ranked, and contracts will be awarded to the five top-ranked bidders. Any requirements for consultants will then be competed amongst each of the contractors holding a contract. Bidders awarded a contract under the PSSC must provide consultants on an as-and-when requested basis, mainly for the CRA’s Information Technology Branch (ITB) within the National Capital Region (NCR); however, other branches and locations within the CRA may also make use of the PSSC. The work will be either remote or in-person. The period of the Contract is from April 1, 2027 to March 31, 2029 inclusive with options to extend the term of the contract by up to three additional one-year periods under the same conditions. The table below summarizes the total invoiced amounts under the Professional Services Supply Chain for the past three calendar years. January 1 – December 31 2023 - $61,283,633.32 January 1 – December 21 2024 - $41,421,783.98 January 1 – December 31 2025 - $15,606,254.92 As part of the Government of Canada’s (GC) continued commitment to responsible fiscal management, Budget 2023 announced significant reductions in discretionary spending on consulting, other professional services, and travel. The GC implemented $500 million in reductions in 2023-24, with ongoing annual reductions of $1.7 billion starting in 2024-25. Consequently, the CRA anticipates a continued decline in professional services procurement as it continues to realign resources to higher-priority areas. As the refocusing of GC spending is an ongoing process, however, the CRA is unable to quantify the extent of these reductions at this time. There are security requirements associated with this requirement. For additional information, consult the bid solicitation document. This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers and to bidders of an applicable trading partner. For additional information, consult the bid solicitation document. The Policy on Prioritizing Canadian Suppliers and Canadian Content in Strategic Federal Procurements will be applied to contracts awarded pursuant to this solicitation. The Federal Contractors Program (FCP) for employment equity applies to this procurement. Proposal documents and supporting information must be submitted in either English or French. The CRA reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Questions must be directed in writing to the contracting authority via email: Karan.Beaulieu@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids must be submitted by using the Connect service provided by the Canada Post Corporation. When responding, the proposal MUST be delivered to: Canada Revenue Agency Bid Receiving Unit BRUg@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids will not be accepted if emailed directly to this email address. title: Languages Testing for Interpreters
description: Services Requirement This requirement is for: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada Title: 20260726-IRB – Language Testing for Interpreters Description of the Requirement: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada has a requirement for service of testing components and test assessments for the recruitment of their interpreter contractors to Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (IRB). Interpreter Services Contractors (ISCs) accredited by the IRB must successfully complete three (3) language tests with a minimum score of 70% to qualify for a contract: • Official Languages Test: Assesses the applicant’s ability to communicate in English or French. This is the first test administered, consisting of a short 15-minute written assessment designed to evaluate comprehension in one of the official languages. • Hearing Simulation (Oral) Test: Evaluates the applicant’s ability to perform consecutive interpretation between an official language and a target language, and vice versa. These tests are currently available in sixty (60) languages. However, there are only two versions of each language test, and the quality and consistency of the tests vary. • Sight Translation Test: Measures the applicant’s ability to translate short documents similar to those that may be presented in a hearing room from the language of interpretation to English or French. This is the final test administered. Level of Security Requirement: Resource(s) Minimum Security Level Required is Reliability Status. Associated Documents: Request for Proposal (RFP) 20260726-IRB. Proposed period of contract: The proposed period of contract shall be from September 30, 2026, to March 31, 2027. The resulting contract will include three (3) one-year optional periods. Estimated Level of Effort: The overall annual cumulative estimated level of effort of the contract(s) will be for 300 tests. Multiple contracts: Considering that contract(s) will be issue based on offerors qualified language(s), this solicitation could results on multiples contracts. title: Chemical Residue and Allergen Testing in and on Food Products for Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA)
description: AMENDMENT TO CLOSING TIME: Please disregard the Ariba Discovery posting response deadline closing time and Buyandsell posting closing time. All required supporting documentation and bid submission must be submitted by 2026-10-16 at 2 p.m. EST. All bids submitted after 2 p.m. EST will result in the bid being declared non-responsive. This solicitation is for the requirement of analytical and laboratory services for the testing of chemical contaminants and/or allergens in foods, food crops, and tissues of food animals for the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA). Multiple contracts will be established as a result of this solicitation. The requirement is divided into two distinct parts. Part A: Categorized by commodity/food group for a total of 7 food groups (Dairy, Eggs, Fish & Seafood, Fresh Fruit & Vegetables, Honey, Meat, and Processed Products). Part B: Categorized by testing programs for a total of 24 programs (including 3-MCPD, Arsenic, BPA, Alternaria, Benzopyrene, etc.). An Offeror may submit an offer for one or multiple food groups in Part A and/or for one or more testing programs in Part B. Contracts awarded to bidders for multiple food groups and/or programs will be consolidated into a single contract. The full Submission of Offers and annexes can only be accessed and downloaded when logged into your SAP Ariba account and your Government of Canada profile has been approved by SAP Ariba. For technical support with SAP Ariba, please contact the CanadaBuys Service Desk.

title: Light Forces Enhancement
description: W8476-206234/C Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is requesting Industry feedback regarding the Light Forces Enhancement (LFE) project for the Government of Canada (GC), the Department of National Defence (DND), and the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF). The Canadian Light Forces (LF) need new light tactical personnel and cargo carrying capabilities. These capabilities will move soldiers and equipment across complex terrain which currently can only be reached on foot. It will lighten CAF soldiers’ on-person combat burden by carrying additional equipment and supplies, and will cover a larger area of operation through increased speed, range, and duration. This powerful, lightweight solution is expected to operate in domestic and expeditionary deployments, up to and including high threat environments. Related Notices: LFE RFI/A https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/pw-bl-319-28038 LFE RFI/B https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/pw-bl-319-29019

title: ITQ for iCDPSC (W8703-270048)
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada, on behalf of the Department of National Defence, invites suppliers to respond to this Invitation to Qualify (ITQ), which will qualify suppliers to participate in future procurement processes regarding the Interim Canadian Deep Precision Strike Capability (iCDPSC). The Department of National Defence has a requirement to establish the Initial Operational Capability of the Canadian Deep Precision Strike Capability. The requirement includes an initial quantity of land-based launch systems, system support services, conventional precision-guided munitions, mission-planning and command-and control systems, communications, support equipment, training, documentation, maintenance and technical support. The interim capability must be deployable, survivable, interoperable with Canadian and allied forces, and capable of delivering precise effects at extended ranges in contested operational environments. This ITQ is open to Canadian Suppliers and suppliers of the Five Eyes Alliance, the NATO community, and Ukraine.

This RFI is on behalf of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Office of Chief Information Officer. THIS IS A RFI ONLY. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research purposes in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10. This RFI does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or other solicitation. The Government is under no obligation to issue a solicitation, award a contract, or reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting responses. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party's expense. Responses will be used to assist the Government in acquisition planning, market research, and requirements development. The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. All submissions become the property of the Government and will not be returned. If you submit proprietary information, you must clearly mark �PROPRIETARY� on every sheet containing such information and segregate the proprietary information to the maximum extent practical from other portions of your response (e.g., use an attachment or exhibit). Respondents are responsible for adequately marking proprietary information in their response. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked �Proprietary� will be handled accordingly. At the sole discretion of the Government, the Government may select several vendors that will be invited to one-on-one sessions with the agency to demonstrate their product and/or services. Vendors who submit responses that are not responsive to this RFI or are outside the scope of what is being requested, will not be considered for one-on-one sessions. Response Due Date: October 16, 2026 @ 10:00 AM, EDT The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) for market research purposes. ICE is seeking information from industry regarding capable vendors who can provide services across three functional areas supporting the ICE OCIO to help drive purposeful, mission enablement: Artificial Intelligence Data Technology Strategy / Architecture These functional areas provide platforms, architecture, standards, governance, strategy, and priority solutions relating to AI, data, and technology enablement across the ICE enterprise - AI Data Technology Strategy (ADTS).

title: Role Player Support
description: The purpose of this notice is to issue Amendment 0001 to Request for Quotation (RFQ) / Solicitation H9224026QE075 for Role Player Support Services. This procurement is conducted as a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Set-Aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 611699 (All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction). The purpose of this solicitation amendment is to: 1 Extend Proposal Submission Date: Extend proposal submission date to 16 Oct 2026, 10:00 AM ET. 2. Revise Solicitation Sections: Revise Section L (FAR 52.212-1 Addendum) and Section M (FAR 52.212-2 Addendum) to incorporate changes resulting from Q&A as well as make administrative corrections. 3. Notice that FAR 52.228-5 (Insurance - Work on a Government Installation) will be incorporated upon contract award. 4. Post Government Responses to Vendor Questions (Q&A): Publish the compiled Question and Answer (Q&A) document. (Note: Access must be requested via SAM.gov in the same manner as the CUI PWS). 5. Incorporate Revised Attachment 1: Incorporate revised Attachment 1 � Performance Work Statement (PWS) - Role Player Support Service. (Controlled Unclassified Information - CUI) 6. Incorporate Revised Attachment 2: Incorporate revised Attachment 2 � Pricing and ELIN Sheet. 7. Incorporate Wage Determinations: Incorporate Attachments 5 through 8 (Wage Determinations for Niland, San Clemente, Ft. Hunter, and Seal Beach, respectively). 8. Incorporate Revised Attachment S.2: Incorporate revised Attachment S.2 � Initial Task Order Request Niland (formerly titled "Sample TOR"). 9. Incorporate Attachment S.3: Incorporate Attachment S.3 � Initial Task Order Request SCI (San Clemente Island). 2. CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION (CUI) & CONTROLLED DOCUMENT ACCESS INSTRUCTIONS CRITICAL NOTICE TO OFFERORS: Certain solicitation documents including the Q&A document, the revised Attachment 1 (Performance Work Statement - PWS), and associated task order technical exhibits contain Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) or controlled procurement details. Offerors shall request access to the Q&A document, revised CUI Attachment 1 � Performance Work Statement (PWS) - Role Player Support Service, and applicable controlled attachments directly through SAM.gov under this solicitation listing. Explicit Request Required: Offerors will not be able to download the Q&A document or the revised CUI Attachment 1 � Performance Work Statement (PWS) - Role Player Support Service directly without requesting and receiving approved access through SAM.gov. Eligibility Requirements: Access will only be granted to interested vendors with an active SAM.gov registration, verified CAGE Code, documented authorization/need-to-know, and verified eligibility under the SDVOSB set-aside under NAICS 611699. Processing Time: Offerors are strongly advised to submit access requests through SAM.gov immediately. Please allow sufficient time for the Contracting Activity to verify credentials and process authorizations. Delays in requesting access do not constitute grounds for an extension of the proposal submission deadline. Handling & Safeguarding: All CUI and controlled materials provided must be stored, handled, transmitted, and destroyed in strict compliance with DoD CUI policy and applicable federal guidelines. 3. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS & ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF AMENDMENT Revised Submission Deadline: All proposals/quotes must be received no later than 16 Oct 2026 at 10:00 AM ET. Submission Method: Proposals shall be delivered in accordance with the updated instructions in Section L (FAR 52.212-1 Addendum). Late submissions will be handled in accordance with FAR 52.212-1(f). If an Offeror�s proposal is marked as or contains Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), the proposal shall not be transmitted via standard unencrypted email. Instead, the Offeror must contact the Contracting Officer (KO) by email no later than [e.g., 48 hours] prior to the proposal submission deadline to formally request a secure upload link via the DoD SAFE (Secure Access File Exchange) service. The Government will provide a one-time link to the Offeror for the secure transmission of its CUI-marked proposal. It is the Offeror's responsibility to request this link in a timely manner to ensure its proposal is submitted by the required deadline. Any proposal containing CUI that is transmitted through unsecure means may be rejected and may not be considered for evaluation. Acknowledgment of Amendments: In accordance with solicitation terms and FAR provisions, Offerors shall acknowledge receipt of Amendment 0001 by signing and returning a complete Standard Form 30 (SF-30) with proposal submission. This solicitation is set aside exclusively for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB). The objective of this requirement is to provide realistic role player support services in support of the Naval Special Warfare Command (NSWC) enterprise. These critical role player services include routine unit-level training exercises as well as periodic, short-notice advanced training exercises, both designed to replicate the complex tactical environments and scenarios encountered by Special Operations Forces (SOF). Role player requirements span eight distinct categories, including specialized linguists, tactical opposing forces (OPFOR), amputee role players, and pyrotechnic/weapons subject matter experts. Offerors are strictly required to read all solicitation documents in full to ensure complete proposal submission compliance. Attachment 1 - Performance Work Statement (PWS) contains Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). Due to strict security and dissemination controls, the PWS is password-protected. Prospective offerors shall email the Contracting Point of Contact, Emily Lonigro, at Emily.Lonigro@socom.mil to obtain the access password. All email requests shall explicitly reference solicitation number H9224026QE075 and shall include the requesting firm's Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code as well as their SAM Unique Entity ID (UEI). Offerors shall submit written questions during the quote and proposal preparation period utilizing Attachment S-1 - Q&A. All questions shall be received no later than 10:00 AM Eastern Time (ET) on 24 September 2026, as only written questions will receive a formal response. To ensure a timely and precise response from the government, each submitted question shall include the document name, document date, specific page, paragraph, clause, or other definitive citation requiring clarification. Final quotes shall be submitted no later than 10:00 AM Eastern Time (ET) on 14 October 2026. Quotes shall remain valid for no less than 180 days from the date of the RFQ closing.

title: Request for Information/Market Intelligence Notice: Microgrid Projects � Use of Progressive Design Build (PDB) with Other Transaction Authority (OTA)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE: This is a request for information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a solicitation or a request for proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS CODE: 237130 Power and Communication Line and Related Structures Construction SMALL BUSINESS STANDARD: $45,000,000.00 NOTE: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base. PROGRAM/PROJECT OVERVIEW: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, has a requirement to execute the construction of microgrids that will provide emergency support to all Installation Energy and Water Plans (IEWP) and critical facilities for 14+ calendar days in the event of a utility grid outage. The Government is evaluating the feasibility of executing these requirements via Progressive Design-Build (PDB) utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The Louisville District is considering the PDB OTA approach for various microgrid projects within the continental United States. Summaries of potential projects being considered for this acquisition strategy are as follows: Fort Sill Power Generation & Microgrid, Ft. Sill, Oklahoma: Design and construction of a microgrid on Fort Sill powered by a new black start capable 18MW natural gas reciprocating internal combustion engine (RICE) power plant. The plant will be required to limit its potential to emit to maintain the installation�s existing synthetic minor air permit. The microgrid will provide emergency support to a portion of the critical facilities for 14+ days in the event of a utility grid outage. During a utility grid outage, the microgrid, energized by the 18MW natural gas RICE plant, will island a portion of the installation from the grid, shed non-critical loads where economically feasible, and provide support to the IEWP identified critical facilities within the islanded area. The microgrid will consist of the following: An 18MW natural gas RICE plant located within one or more weather-protective shelters on an elevated plot of open land to the southeast of building 3933. An electrical interconnection of the new RICE plant to an existing electrical substation. A natural gas pipeline to connect the RICE plant to the natural gas infrastructure. Modifications to the existing substation. A microgrid control system with fiber optic and other communications infrastructure to control the various components. Underground utilities and site work features such as grading, drainage, pads, access drive, site lighting, and perimeter fence. Camp Parks Reserve Forces Training Area (PRFTA) Microgrid and Power Generation, Camp Parks, California: Expand an existing microgrid to provide resilient power for the entire peak critical load of Camp Parks Reserve Forces Training Area (PRFTA). Project will include natural gas generators with a total of 1650KW total capacity, 5,000KWH Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), microgrid, transformers, controls, switches, and a medium voltage distribution system. The project will also include utilities, additional underground electrical distribution system, site improvements, communication infrastructure, and integration with the existing Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system. The microgrid will integrate the existing 2,100KWac solar PV arrays and 2,332 KWh BESS to provide resilient power for the peak load demand at PRFTA. INFORMATION REQUESTED: Interested industry partners are requested to respond to the following questions to help shape the final acquisition strategy: Company Profile: Q1. Business Name Q2. Address Q3. Point of Contract (Name, Title) Q4. Phone Number Q5. Email Address Q6. Unique Entity ID Q7. Cage Code Q8. Socioeconomic Status (Other Than Small, Small, 8(a), SDVOSB, etc.) Q9. Participating Role (Prime Contractor, Subcontractor, Design Firm, Other) Other Transaction Authority (OTA) & Statutory Compliance: Q10. OTA Experience � Describe your firm�s previous experience, if any, executing projects utilizing OTA. Q11. What project characteristics make PDB OTA particularly advantageous or disadvantageous for this requirement? Progressive Design-Build (PDB) / Early Contractor Involvement: Q12. What minimum level of detail (e.g., Statement of Need, conceptual site plans, target budget) does your firm require prior to entering Phase 1 (Design/Pre-construction) to feel confident in the project's viability? Q13. What collaborative mechanisms (such as joint design charrettes, target-value design workshops, or phased scoping approvals) do you recommend the Government implement in the first 30-90 days to rapidly transition from a "blank page" to a mutually agreed-upon baseline? Q14. Describe your experience executing Progressive Design-Build, Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR), or other highly collaborative delivery methods where designer and builder worked collaboratively with the owner before locking in a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). Feedback on the Acquisition Strategy & Alternatives: Q15. Does the proposed PDB-OTA strategy incentivize your firm to participate? Why or why not? Q16. Are there alternative acquisition strategies, commercial phasing arrangements, or risk-sharing terms that the Government has not considered that would yield a higher quality facility, faster delivery, or lower cost? Bonding Capability: Q17. Specify your maximum bonding (single and aggregate) as a sole prime contractor and/or as a joint venture. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: Please submit your responses by 16 October 2026 at 1000 hrs Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) to MAJ Lesa Sylve at lesa.b.sylve@usace.army.mil. The Government welcomes candid industry feedback and recommendations regarding commercial practices, agreement terms, project phasing, risk sharing, governance, pricing approaches, and other considerations that could improve successful execution of these projects under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Interested firms are encouraged to add themselves to the Interested Vendors List associated with this announcement on SAM.gov to receive future updates. Note: Do not submit proprietary trade secrets, protected technologies, or classified information in your response. All feedback received will be handled as public market research to shape the Government's final acquisition approach.

description: **NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE** This is a Notice of Intent to Sole Source published in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) RFO 5.101(a) Presolicitation notice requirements and (FAR) RFO 12.102 Restricting Competition. This Notice of Intent is for a proposed award of an open market sole source award to Evoqua Water Technologies, LLC for an annual service contract for the six WRO300H Reverse Osmosis Dialysis Water System units currently in use at the VA Maryland Health Care System (VAMHCS) Baltimore VAMC 10 North Greene St. Baltimore, MD 21201. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this service is 221310 (Water Supply and Irrigation Systems). Product Service Code (PSC) is J046 (Maintenance, Repair and Rebuilding of Equipment Water Purification and Sewage Treatment Equipment. Small business size standard is $36.0 Million. While this synopsis does not constitute a solicitation, interested vendors may identify their interest and capability to satisfy the requirement. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency, by emailing such statement and supporting documentation by NLT 10:00 AM Eastern Standard Time (EST), 10/16/2026 to Contract Specialist Patricia Thai via email at Patricia.Thai@va.gov. Please reference the announcement number (36C24527Q0030) in the subject line of the e-mail. Such documentation will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct the procurement on a competitive basis. A determination not to compete this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government under authorities cited above. Statement of Work Scope of Work: The vendor will provide support for the six WRO300H reverse osmosis dialysis water system units listed below that are currently in use at the Baltimore VA Medical Center. The Contractor shall maintain the Mar Cor reverse osmosis dialysis water system machines in proper operating condition and assure optimum performance and reliability as well as the overall safety of the patients.� The Contractor will provide all the parts and services necessary for the maintenance and repair of the provided reverse osmosis units. Service coverage must include replacement parts such as filters, repairs, preventative maintenance service and other incidentals necessary to perform scheduled preventive maintenance and to restore the covered equipment to operating specifications in accordance with the manufacturer s specifications throughout the term of the contract. The contractor shall report to Biomedical Engineering upon arriving on-site at the Baltimore VAMC, before performing any maintenance. The equipment requires a service contract to ensure that the reverse osmosis units are properly maintained and are safe and functional for use and patient care. Additionally, the contractor must provide software and quality updates, technical and clinical application support by telephone, and remote monitoring and diagnostic support to minimize unexpected equipment downtime and maximize use of the equipment. The vendor must have an approved MOU/ISA with the Department of Veterans Affairs to provide remote support. The vendor will supply the Baltimore VAMC Biomedical Engineering department with a copy of a detailed service report that meets the requirements of 21CFR820, subpart N, within 2 weeks of maintenance being completed. The service shall be performed between the hours of 7:00am and 4:00pm, Monday through Friday, unless mutually agreed upon by the contractor and the VA Biomedical Engineering department. The contractor shall schedule all maintenance with Biomedical Engineering and report to Biomedical Engineering in room 5B-183 upon arriving on-site at the Baltimore VAMC, before performing any maintenance. The Contractor shall ensure all maintenance services performed are fully documented (service reports) and will supply the Baltimore VAMC Biomedical Engineering Department with a detailed service report to include the following information: Model and serial number of equipment serviced Name of the technician Date and time called, time of arrival, point of contact, and reason for call Description of� all work performed, and identification of all parts replaced including part numbers and serial numbers Written procedures followed and evidence that equipment has been inspected, calibrated, and retested/certified according to those procedures Provision and placement of labels on the part and machine to indicate that the item/machine was serviced Below is the list of equipment identified to be covered by this service contract: Mar Cor WRO300H Reverse Osmosis Dialysis Water Systems SN s Coverage Monday Friday, 7am-4pm Two business day system replacement warranty 24/7/365 remote technical support with 30-minute response time Software and quality updates Online clinical continuing education for imaging professionals Uptime commitment of 95% Preform a quarterly performance review Inspect and replace all filters quarterly Background: The VA Maryland Health Care System requires full-service coverage of the WROH 300 reverse osmosis dialysis water systems that are utilized at the Baltimore VA Medical Center. This service coverage includes replacement parts, repairs and scheduled preventive maintenance in accordance with the manufacturer s recommendations to ensure that the equipment is properly maintained and to reduce downtime of the identified equipment that results in cancellations of patient appointments. Performance Period: 1 year from time of award Type of Contract: Maintenance services Place of Performance: Baltimore VA Medical Center 10 N. Greene St Baltimore, MD 21201 Performance Based Contract: N/A Security: The contractor must have photo ID available when performing work at a VA Medical Center and be willing to present it to VA staff. The vendor is responsible for personal protective equipment.

title: S201--NFS Deep cleaning (VA-27-00008465)
description: Recurring Kitchen Deep Cleaning Services Washington DC VA Medical Center (DCVAMC) NAICS: 561720 Janitorial Services THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION 1. Purpose The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Strategic Acquisition Office (SAO East), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify qualified and capable sources for recurring kitchen deep cleaning services, performed twice per month (24 service visits per year) for the Nutrition and Food Service (NFS) kitchen(s) at the Washington DC VA Medical Center (DCVAMC), 50 Irving Street NW, Washington, DC 20422. This RFI is strictly for market research and does not obligate the Government to award a contract. 2. Background DCVAMC requires comprehensive, recurring deep cleaning to maintain a clean, sanitary, and inspection ready kitchen environment that reduces grease buildup, protects food preparation areas, and supports compliance with health and sanitation standards (including readiness for routine health department and Joint Commission inspections). Services will be scheduled approximately every two weeks and performed during off hours to minimize disruption. 3. Anticipated Requirements & Required Capabilities Respondents should demonstrate the ability to perform turn key twice monthly deep cleaning services covering, at a minimum, the tasks and standards below: 3.1 Task Coverage Tile Floor Degreasing & Deep Cleaning: Use food safe, non corrosive, EPA registered solutions; commercial grade scrubbers/rotary machines; special attention to grout lines, corners/edges, and accessible areas beneath equipment. Stainless Steel Cleaning & Polishing: Thorough detailing and polishing of accessible stainless surfaces (countertops, workstations, shelving exteriors, sinks), including equipment legs/frames/casters and under/around prep areas. Sanitization & High Touch Points: Sanitize food prep surfaces with appropriate EPA registered solutions; clean baseboards/corners, doors, kick plates, handles, switches; perform trash removal and detail accessible hard to reach areas. 3.2 Explicit Exclusions Interiors of stainless cabinets, dishwashers, ovens, and freezers are excluded from this recurring scope; they may be requested separately under additional authorization/pricing. 3.3 Equipment & Materials Contractor furnishes all equipment, cleaning solutions/degreasers (food safe, EPA registered), mops/brushes/towels/polishing consumables; provide SDS to COR prior to first visit and upon changes. No Government furnished equipment. 3.4 Scheduling & Service Windows Frequency: Twice per month (24 visits/year); scheduled at ~two week intervals. Coordination: Schedule each visit with COR at least 5 business days in advance; adjust dates that conflict with Federal holidays or kitchen operations within the same cycle. Service Hours: Off hours or as designated by COR to avoid meal service. 3.5 Quality Control & Inspection Maintain a Quality Control Program; COR inspects after each visit. Contractor corrects deficiencies within 24 hours at no additional cost; repeated failures may result in contract action. Provide a service completion checklist after each visit. 3.6 Safety & Compliance Comply with applicable OSHA (29 CFR Parts 1910 and 1926), DCVAMC infection control, fire safety, and security requirements; use EPA registered chemicals suitable for food contact surfaces; place wet floor signs during/after floor cleaning. Complete an ICRA (Infection Control Risk Assessment) approved by Infection Control before starting the initial service; ensure all personnel meet VA facility access/badging requirements. 3.7 Personnel & Labor Standards Provide sufficient trained personnel in commercial kitchen cleaning, food safe chemical handling, and healthcare protocols; designate an on site supervisor/team lead each visit. Personnel are subject to applicable SCA Wage Determination requirements for the Washington, DC area. 3.8 Period of Performance (Anticipated) One Year. Final POP date will be set at award; this RFI is to assess market capabilities and pricing insights only. 4. Requested Information from Vendors Please submit a capability package that includes: Company Information: Name; UEI; socio economic status under NAICS 561720; primary POC (name, title, phone, email). Capabilities & Approach: Narrative describing how you will meet sections 3.1 3.7, including equipment/chemicals (EPA registered products), staffing/training, quality control, safety/infection control procedures (ICRA), and scheduling. Past Performance: Up to three (3) relevant projects for recurring commercial kitchen deep cleaning in healthcare or similar high compliance environments, including scope, frequency, locations, contract values, and COR/POC contact details. Contract Vehicles: Any VA relevant vehicles (e.g., IDIQs) or other vehicles through which services could be ordered. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) Pricing (Non Binding): Monthly price for twice per month visits (Base Year assumption). Any assumptions (hours, crew size, equipment). Optional prompt payment or volume discounts. (ROM is for budgeting/market research only and will not be evaluated as a proposal.) Site Access & Badging: Confirmation of ability to meet VA access/badging and background investigation requirements for all personnel. 5. Submission Instructions Due Date/Time: Wednesday, October 16, 2026, 10:00 AM ET Submission Method: Email responses (PDF or Word) to: cassie.white@va.gov Cassie A. White Contract Specialist, SAO East Email: cassie.white@va.gov Subject Line: RFI Response DCVAMC Kitchen Deep Cleaning [Your Company Name] . 6. Additional Notes Site Visits: Not anticipated for this RFI. If a future solicitation is issued, site visits may be coordinated at that time. Set Aside: Undetermined at this time; results may inform acquisition strategy. 7. Disclaimer This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes it does not constitute a solicitation and does not commit the Government to any contract or acquisition. The Government will not reimburse costs incurred for responding to this notice. Do not submit proposals at this time.
